why: THE MEANEST BRACKET 4 EDGAR — the pilot's profile, in his words (2026-10-19): a vampire deck that feels fast, threatening, bracket 4; life gain + life drain is the core mechanic; ways of transforming vampire tokens into bigger threats; targeted removal; interaction and card draw are critical; once the combo pieces come out the table targets the vamps, so as much protection and interaction as possible. THE PROFILE, not a gate (the pilot: 'we need to stop gating changes on a single metric'): judged on the whole paired net-change table and the rating's component deltas — damage @T8/@T10 and board power @T6 (fast, threatening, tokens into threats); the goldfish's cumulative drain by T8/T10 and life gained (the core, read from goldfish_metrics branch vs champion until a net-change row carries it); interaction affordable @T6, the audit's interaction (10, at), interaction-breadth (3 of 5, under) and protection (9, over) and the rating's resilience component (targeted removal, protection); extra cards @T8 and the audit's card-advantage (8, under) — the running-out-of-steam axis. The ONE pre-registered row is a GUARD, not the goal: extra cards by T8 may not fall below the champion's 1.68. Keep list: Vish Kal, Bloodthirsty Conqueror, Vito, Sanguine Bond, Exquisite Blood. Built from the watch sets deckcheck-mean-v1 (eleven) and deckcheck-tune-v1 (five), slot by slot with the pilot before staging. Objective rewritten 2026-10-19 before anything was staged or measured (it read kill_by_8 >= 0.75 when opened on 2026-10-18).
